newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian investigators probe Milan bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Italian investigators probe Milan bomb attack.

text.p: Italian investigators opened a probe on Saturday into a bombing that ripped a hole in Milan's city hall before key municipal elections on Sunday.
No one was injured in the blast, which blew open the back wall of the city hall, partially damaged the council chamber and shattered windows in adjacent buildings early on Friday.
Milan prosecutors met on Saturday to begin their probe into the attack, carried out before elections in which the post of mayor of Italy's financial capital will be the biggest prize.
Italian television said investigators were looking into the possibility that an anarchist group called "Revolutionary Action" planted the bomb.

The Italian news agency ANSA said it had received a phone call late on Friday claiming the group, which operated in Italy when the country was afflicted by terrorism in the late 1970s, was responsible for the bomb attack.

ANSA quoted the anonymous caller as saying: "You have not understood anything about the attack we have made on Milan city hall. It was aimed at parliament which we feel is merely the political arm of the bourgeoisie."
The caller added that the group "wanted the liberation of all anarchists who have been arrested...otherwise you will pay the consequences".
A device was also found on Friday outside the office of a local radio station. The metal tube, hidden in a bag, carried the words "Don't Vote" and was signed "Revolutionary Action".
Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said the device, consisting of gunpowder and bolts packed into a steel container and left on a windowsill, had been powerful enough to kill.
"It shows that at this moment there are hotbeds of violence in Italian society that we have to confront," he said.

Politicians from across the main spectrum said the choice of date and the timing ahead of Sunday's municipal elections in Milan and more than 1,000 other towns and cities appeared to be an act of intimidation.

The race for mayor of Milan is the highest profile contest in Sunday's local elections, the biggest test of voter support since Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left Olive Tree coalition won a general election victory on April 21 last year.
